speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many PMETs have been assisted under the Career Support Programme (CSP) since its inception, with a breakdown by each of the three six-monthly employment period and by those aged above and below 40 respectively; (b) what evidence is available indicating that the PMETs have been successfully reintegrated into the workforce with the help of this scheme; and (c) whether any evidence has emerged indicating gaps in the employability of PMETs under the CSP that require further training interventions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: This helps to address mismatches in wage expectations and provides mid-career PMET job-seekers more opportunities to regain employment, especially the long-term unemployed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: The CSP also helps employers to tap a wider pool of mid-career PMETs to meet their manpower needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: In fact, around half of CSP employers are small and mediaum enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: The retention rate of the 2015 and 2016 cohorts is encouraging.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: Majority remained with the CSP employer and the rest found new jobs with other employers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: Those who are still seeking employment can return to Workforce Singapore (WSG) or NTUC-e2i centres for assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: Apart from CSP, PMET job seekers can also benefit from other Adapt and Grow programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: For example, PMETs with skills mismatches can tap on the Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) to reskill and move into new occupations and sectors with good prospects and opportunities for progression.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: Momentum for the PCPs has also picked up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister of Manpower)
text: In the first three quarters of 2017, about 2,700 PMETs were placed under the PCPs, and this is up from 900 in the same period in 2016.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If I understood the Minister correctly, to date, for the CSP about 70% of the employees have remained in the CSP employer, and 30% have moved on to another employer, or have left the CSP employer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Deputy Speaker, to clarify, 70% remained in employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But as it turns out, of those who remained in employment, 70% remained with the same employer and 30% moved on to another employer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But so as not to confused matters, we just stick to 70% remained in employment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, my supplementary question will be, to date, based on these figures, I suppose a minority of them, I mean there was a certain amount of attrition – about 30% – have there been any insights gleaned into the reasons behind that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Were there any employability gaps that were discerned after the PMET was placed with the CSP employer which suggest that there are some training gaps that need to be fulfilled?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Because anecdotally, I have come across such feedback that that may be the case occasionally.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And if so, what kind of solutions can be put forward or deployed to meet those training and employability gaps.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Obviously, the needs differ, and so, we do not use one programme exclusively.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of the CSP, it is very targeted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the person is more or less job ready.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The employer is quite keen to take him or her on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the salary remains something that they cannot find agreement on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the CSP comes in specifically to address this issue.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) addresses a different set of issues.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Under those circumstances, the jobseeker may be attractive to the employer, but there is a certain gap in the range of skills that he has that causes the employer to think a little bit harder.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, the PCP comes in to intervene and encourages the employer to give the jobseeker an opportunity to close that skills gap.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, CSP takes care of wage gap; PCP takes care of skills gap.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Within the whole range of programmes under the Adapt and Grow Initiative, there are yet others.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the P-Max programme deals specifically with the needs of SMEs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For some PMETs that are transiting from different work environments, the cultural context of operating in an SME may require them to have a longer period of adjustment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should add that at the Careers Connect centres, which WSG operates, there are a whole range of other programmes that deal specifically with issues that jobseekers may have, and they are not confined to training intervention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, for example, there may be jobseekers who are struggling to cope emotionally with job loss and they have to cross that barrier before they be effective in job search.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Career Recharger programme does that for them – it is one-on-one counselling.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are those who have overcome that barrier, but they want to share tips with other jobseekers who are looking for work in the same field.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Career 360 programme does that for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, there may be those who have not quite sorted out what they really want to do at that stage of their career.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Career Catalyst programme again provides one-on-one counselling to help them to do that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there are a whole range of programmes available, and we remain very open to what other interventions will help jobseekers regain employment more quickly, and we will continue to improve upon them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To his question, if I understand correctly, on whether we can detect that a person has been employed and so, automatically provide a CSP assistance to his employer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The difficulty with that is: how do we know that there was a wage gap?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is only when, if the person has been employed, one assumes that the employer was happy to pay whatever was finally agreed upon.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is not something that we can presume, and there are so many cases where people have entered into jobs, and the employers are happy to settle on a certain level of payment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we should not assume that there was a wage gap to begin with.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time I think, given what has been discussed in this House in the last couple of days, when disbursing grants, even in terms of wage support, we want to make sure that it is in cases that are really deserving.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Can we improve on the application and the processing; can we make sure the employer does not have to wait too long?
